```{ojs}
//| echo: false
solowDiagram = Plot.plot({
  width: 460,
  height: 360,
  x: {label: "k", domain: [0, kMax]},
  y: {label: perWorker},
  color: {
    legend: true,
    domain: ["investment, s·f(k)", "break-even investment"],
    range: [colours.investment, colours.breakEven]
  },
  marks: [
    Plot.ruleY([0]),
    Plot.ruleX([kStar], {strokeDasharray: "3,3", strokeOpacity: 0.6}),
    // The investment curve in force now, and the other regime's curve dashed.
    hasShock ? Plot.line(grid, {x: "k", y: shocked ? "investmentBefore" : "investmentAfter", stroke: colours.investment, strokeDasharray: "4,3", strokeOpacity: 0.5}) : null,
    Plot.line(grid, {x: "k", y: shocked ? "investmentAfter" : "investmentBefore", stroke: () => "investment, s·f(k)"}),
    Plot.line(grid, {x: "k", y: "breakEven", stroke: () => "break-even investment"}),
    // Current capital stock, and the gap between the curves that drives it.
    Plot.ruleX([now.k], {y1: 0, y2: Math.min(investmentNow, breakEvenNow), strokeOpacity: 0.4}),
    Plot.ruleX([now.k], {y1: breakEvenNow, y2: investmentNow, stroke: colours.gap, strokeWidth: 3}),
    Plot.dot([now], {x: "k", y: investmentNow, fill: colours.investment, r: 4}),
    Plot.dot([now], {x: "k", y: breakEvenNow, fill: colours.breakEven, r: 4}),
    Plot.dot([now], {x: "k", y: 0, fill: "currentColor", r: 5})
  ]
})

// Time series of one variable: the full path faintly, the part travelled so far
// in bold, and a marker at the current period.
// On a log scale the axis starts at the smallest value rather than zero.
// `rules` are dashed horizontal reference lines, [{x1, x2, y}, ...].
// `key` is a column of `path`, or a function of a row.
function timePlot(key, {label = key, rules = [], log = false, max} = {}) {
  const value = typeof key === "function" ? key : d => d[key]
  if (max === undefined) max = d3.max(path, value)
  const min = log ? d3.min(path, value) : Math.min(0, d3.min(path, value))
  return Plot.plot({
    width: 460,
    height: 360,
    x: {label: "t", domain: [0, periods]},
    y: {label: log ? `${label} (log scale)` : label, type: log ? "log" : "linear", domain: [min, max]},
    marks: [
      Plot.ruleY([log ? min : 0]),
      Plot.ruleY(rules, {x1: "x1", x2: "x2", y: "y", strokeDasharray: "3,3", strokeOpacity: 0.6}),
      hasShock ? Plot.ruleX([shockT], {strokeDasharray: "1,3", strokeOpacity: 0.6}) : null,
      Plot.line(path, {x: "t", y: value, strokeOpacity: 0.2}),
      Plot.line(path.slice(0, t + 1), {x: "t", y: value, strokeWidth: 2}),
      Plot.dot([now], {x: "t", y: value, fill: "currentColor", r: 5})
    ]
  })
}

kStarRules = [
  {x1: 0, x2: shockT, y: kStarBefore},
  {x1: shockT, x2: periods, y: kStarAfter}
]

// In steady state GDP per capita grows at the rate of technology, g (zero if
// technology is constant).
growthRules = [{x1: 0, x2: periods, y: 100 * g}]

html`<div class="sim-grid">
  <div><strong>Solow diagram</strong>${solowDiagram}</div>
  <div><strong>Transition path: capital ${perWorker}, k</strong>${timePlot("k", {max: kMax, rules: kStarRules})}</div>
  <div><strong>GDP per capita, Y / L</strong>${timePlot("yPerCapita", {label: "Y / L", log: logScale})}</div>
  <div><strong>Labour force, L</strong>${timePlot("L", {log: logScale})}</div>
  <div><strong>Capital stock, K</strong>${timePlot("K", {log: logScale})}</div>
  <div><strong>Growth of GDP per capita, % per period</strong>${timePlot(d => 100 * d.yPerCapitaGrowth, {label: "%", rules: growthRules})}</div>
</div>`
```
